Shift the best method’s gradient window down by 0.05 while keeping its slope and temperature fixed, testing whether increased retention resolves its lone critical pair. The 2.66-minute last peak leaves ample room to gain separation without a time penalty.

Return to the best gradient and lower temperature by 5 °C to test selectivity at its lone unresolved pair. Lowering the gradient window caused near-coelution, whereas temperature offers a different selectivity lever with ample room below the 10-minute time threshold.

The critical pair improved from R = 0.43 at 25 °C to 1.07 at 30 °C, so test 35 °C with the best gradient unchanged. This probes whether that trend reaches full resolution while checking for compression of neighboring pairs.

At 30 °C, shifting phi0 from 0.45 to 0.40 nearly merged the critical pair; shifting another 0.05 tests for separation beyond that selectivity crossover. Keep the slope unchanged to isolate the window effect, with ample time margin for increased retention.

Injection 12 reached the maximum CRF, so shorten its gradient by one grid step while holding the window and temperature fixed. This tests whether the run can be accelerated while preserving full resolution, with R = 1.87 providing some margin at the critical pair.
Shorten the fully resolved gradient by another grid step to seek a faster method with CRF 1.000. Monitor the pair whose resolution decreased from 2.37 to 2.12 as tG fell from 12 to 10 minutes.

Test the next shorter gradient to locate the speed limit for full resolution at this window and temperature. The critical pair is now at R = 1.81, so this step may approach or cross the 1.5 threshold; injection 14 remains the fastest fully resolved method tested.

Keep injection 14 as the fastest fully resolved fallback, and test whether cooling restores the critical pair in the six-minute gradient. The window-dependent selectivity crossover suggests lower temperature may separate this pair on the low-organic side, potentially enabling further gradient shortening.

Shorten the fully resolved 25 °C gradient by one grid step to offset the retention increase from cooling. All pairs currently have R ≥ 2.01, providing margin to test a faster method while retaining CRF 1.000.

Test a steeper gradient to shorten late retention, while lowering phi0 to counter the critical pair’s loss of separation at higher organic fractions. Injection 17 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback; monitor both its middle and late critical pairs.

Test a steeper version of injection 4’s fast, nearly resolved method, where the critical pair lies on the opposite side of the solvent-selectivity crossover. This may improve that pair while retaining sufficient separation elsewhere; injection 17 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback.

Reduce injection 18’s gradient steepness by lowering phi1, aiming to restore its two unresolved pairs while retaining a short gradient. This tests whether the lower starting organic fraction can support full resolution near injection 17’s elution time.

Raise temperature to improve the late critical pair and shorten retention, while lowering phi1 to counter the middle pair’s tendency to lose resolution on warming. This tests a nearby route to full resolution with a short gradient; injection 17 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback.

Test the minimum gradient duration at the fastest fully resolved method’s window and temperature to establish its speed boundary. The two pairs near R = 1.6 may fall below threshold; retain injection 17 as the fully resolved fallback if they do.

Test an intermediate starting fraction at 25 °C with a shallow gradient to seek another fully resolved selectivity window. Cooling may separate the pair that nearly coeluted at phi0 = 0.40 and 30 °C; injection 17 remains the fastest confirmed method with CRF 1.000.

Shorten injection 23’s fully resolved gradient by one grid step while keeping its window and temperature fixed. Its critical pair has only R = 1.54, so this tests the local speed boundary; injection 17 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Test a modest slope increase from 0.050 to 0.055 organic fraction per minute relative to injection 17, seeking slightly earlier elution while preserving full resolution. This is a final boundary test with limited resolution margin; injection 17 remains the fastest confirmed method achieving CRF 1.000.
